actions.reason: Tokenizer.load parsed the merges one line at a time in Python, calling map(int, line.split()) and doing a dict store per line. Now it reads the rest of the file once, converts every number with a single map(int, ...) call, and builds the merges dict with dict(zip(pairs, range(256, ...))). The merges and their ids come out the same and in the same order, and an odd count of numbers still raises ValueError. Tokenizer.save's vocab loop now does one dict .get per token, where it used to do a membership test plus an index, and uses a bound append. Outputs are identical, and save_load_ir ratio is 0.9205.

--- a/minbpe/base.py
+++ b/minbpe/base.py
@@ -156,17 +156,19 @@ class Tokenizer:
         # this also means that we couldn't possibly use .vocab in load()
         # because decoding in this way is a lossy operation!
         rendered = {idx: render_token(token) for idx, token in self.vocab.items()}
+        get_children = inverted_merges.get
         lines = []
+        append = lines.append
         for idx, s in rendered.items():
             # find the children of this token, if any
-            if idx in inverted_merges:
+            children = get_children(idx)
+            if children is not None:
                 # if this token has children, render it nicely as a merge
-                idx0, idx1 = inverted_merges[idx]
-                lines.append(f"[{rendered[idx0]}][{rendered[idx1]}] -> [{s}] {idx}\n")
+                append(f"[{rendered[children[0]]}][{rendered[children[1]]}] -> [{s}] {idx}\n")
             else:
                 # otherwise this is leaf token, just print it
                 # (this should just be the first 256 tokens, the bytes)
-                lines.append(f"[{s}] {idx}\n")
+                append(f"[{s}] {idx}\n")
         with open(vocab_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
             f.write("".join(lines))
 
@@ -189,10 +191,11 @@ class Tokenizer:
                 special, special_idx = f.readline().strip().split()
                 special_tokens[special] = int(special_idx)

-                idx += 1

journal.text:
I read minbpe/base.py and went after Tokenizer.load, which parsed merges one line at a time with map(int, line.split()) and a dict store per line. I rewrote it to read the rest of the file once, convert every number with a single map(int, ...) call, and build the merges dict with dict(zip(pairs, range(256, ...))). An odd count of numbers still raises. Two edits, 19 changed lines in one file.

My sandbox run was accepted with identical outputs and builds ok. save_load_ir went from 1687062434 to 1552994406, ratio 0.9205. The other metrics barely moved: train_basic_ir 0.9962, train_regex_ir 1.0007, encode_ir 0.9990, decode_ir 0.9989. I submitted it. It is committed and waiting on independent replays.

I think load was dominated by per-line Python overhead, and batching the int conversion is where the gain came from. Training and encode are untouched by this.

Next I would look at the save side of save_load_ir, which still writes line by line, and check whether the vocab rendering in save is costly.
